enabled.description: Enable or disable the ptp2 service at boot.

interfaces.description: List of network interfaces to use for PTP communication. Must support IEEE 1588 PTP timestamping (PHC).

transport.description: PTP transport mode. Common: 'udp' (IPv4/IPv6 over UDP), 'l2' (raw Ethernet), 'ethernet' (alias for l2).

clock_identity.description: Optional 8-byte clock identity in hex (e.g., '00:1b:2b:ff:fe:3c:4d:5e'). If omitted, derived from MAC address.

domain_number.description: PTP domain number (0–127). Must match across all clocks in the same PTP network.

primary.description: If true, this node will act as the primary (best master) clock on the domain (assuming it meets criteria).

log_file.description: Path to the PTP daemon log file.

announce_interval.description: Interval between Announce messages as power-of-two seconds (e.g., 0 = 1s, -1 = 0.5s, 1 = 2s). Default 0.

sync_interval.description: Interval between Sync messages as power-of-two seconds. Default 0 (1s).

delay_req_timeout.description: Number of missed Delay_Req messages before reselecting master. Range: 1–20.

delay_req_interval.description: Interval between Delay_Req messages as power-of-two seconds. Default 0 (1s).

faulty_path_timeout.description: Seconds before marking a path as faulty (disabled if null).

watchdog_timeout.description: Seconds before the watchdog triggers a restart (0 = disabled).

allow_multiple_domains.description: Allow multiple PTP domains on same network. Enable only if necessary and understood.

fallback_to_generic_phc.description: Allow use of non-PHC (e.g., software timestamped) devices if no hardware PHC available.

initial_offset_ns.description: Initial clock offset (nanoseconds) to apply on startup. Useful for calibration.

extra_options.description: Additional command-line options (e.g., ['-s'] for software timestamping, ['-a'] for auto-selection).

interface_overrides.description: List of per-interface configuration overrides. Each entry configures one interface with specific settings.

priority1.description: Priority1 value (0–254) used in Best Master Clock Algorithm (BMCA). Lower = higher priority.

clock_class.description: Clock class (0–255). Lower values indicate higher-quality clocks (0 = primary reference).

master_offset.description: Initial master offset for this interface (nanoseconds, signed).

log_delay_req_interval.description: Delay request interval as power-of-two seconds.
